Preparation is a combination of imagination and planning. Many lack the imagination to comprehend the risks we face. Western society makes us pretty complacent about how fragile our civilization really is; the many systems that won't work without power, the fragility of our water and food supplies, etc. Detailed planning is also required. Many people go and get a gas generator, but only a 12hr fuel supply. A good prepper understands the risks and has thought through what they need to survive. Daniel Suarez has a great bit in one of his books about preparing for the zombie apocalypse, because if you prepare for that you're prepared for most realistic scenarios by default.

Survival is a totally different skill. While preparation gives you the best chance at survival, actual survival depends on how well you function in a crisis; risk assessment, decision making, ability to stave off or work through panic. You can be as prepared as you want, but every crisis is different and requires the ability to act in a timely fashion.

At times, preparation can actually hinder good decisions. If you think that you're prepared, you may be less likely to bug out if shit goes badly wrong. Conversely, those that fail to prepare may have the timely decision skills and resourcefulness to survive without the resources of the highly prepared. Obviously a combination of these skills is best.

Mike Tyson once said, "Everybody has a plan until they get punched in the mouth." No matter how well you think you've prepared, at some point you're going to have to deal with something you didn't prepare for. The ability to do so is what makes you a survivor. Survivors often prepare, but preppers often don't survive.
